:::{#exm-vcov-singular}
#### A variance matrix that is not positive definite

Let $X_1$ have [variance](#def-variance) $\ss > 0$, and let $X_2 = X_1$.
Every [covariance](#def-cov) in $\vX = \tp{(X_1, X_2)}$ is $\Covs{X_1}{X_1} = \ss$ (@lem-cov-xx), so:

$$
\Varf{\vX} = \ss \pmat{1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1}.
$$

With $\va = \tp{(1, -1)}$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\tp{\va}\Varf{\vX}\va &= \Var{X_1 - X_2} \\
&= \Var{0} \\
&= 0,
\end{aligned}
$$

so $\Varf{\vX}$ is positive semidefinite
but not [positive definite](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-special-matrices.html#def-positive-definite)
(compare [this example](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-special-matrices.html#exm-positive-semidefinite)).
If $X_1$ is [continuous](random-variables.qmd#def-continuous-rv),
$\vX$ has no [joint density](random-variables.qmd#thm-no-joint-density-diagonal).

:::
